answer.why: As an insider I'd tap it at once: 'confirmed and substantive' is exactly the wording of a real appointment, and it tells me the designer knows the service. Minister Salary reads like a clickbait joke, and I've heard that debate at every kopitiam and in every comment section. The insider name promises someone got the details right, and I'd want to see if they did.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical, tabloid-ish game about the ministerial pay debate, probably with a big number on screen and a punchline about being overpaid. I'd expect it to be shallow and a bit cheap, aimed at outsiders, with the whole career built around reaching the top salary. I'd also expect details to be wrong and the tone to be mocking rather than fond.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, in-joke name that points to the stage after probation or acting appointments, when you stop being 'acting' and hold the post in your own right. I'd expect a slower and more accurate simulation of grades, appraisals and postings, with humour that only insiders catch. It may look dull to outsiders, but I'd expect it to be the more authentic game.

RACHEL GOH · THE FINAL POSITION
Lost the Ward

Forty-eight point two percent. You shook every hand in that ward and it was not enough, and it was never going to be about you anyway.

RETIRED AS Permanent Secretary
AT AGE 58
LIFETIME EARNINGS $15.45M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file estimated your potential at Senior Director. You were not told.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: At 27, in The Counter, you chose "Tell them exactly why it will fail." It raised your ceiling to Permanent Secretary, the top of the service.
EXPOSURE: Your file is clean enough to be boring. In this building, that is a compliment.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
